en: The Triplet of the Wholesome (Kusalattika) and the Two Triplets of the Internal (Ajjhattattikadvaya).
An unwholesome internal state is a condition for a wholesome internal state by way of object-condition.
(Abbreviated. There are eighteen [conditions] in the case of the object; sixteen in the case of predominance; eighteen in the case of decisive support;
and nine each in the cases of prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.
An unwholesome state that is not external is a condition, by way of object-condition, for an external wholesome state.
(Abbreviated. There are eighteen [conditions] in the case of the object; six in the case of predominance; eighteen in the case of decisive support;
nine in the cases of prenascence, presence, and non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor has an internal object, there arises a neutral state with an internal object by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.

Dependent on a state that is neither wholesome nor has an external object, there arises a neutral state with an external object by way of root-condition. (Abbreviated. Three under root; ... pe ... three under non-disappearance.
